openings.claim: Test allocation mismatch versus compatible-capacity scarcity, including whether elicited flexibility combined with protected 60-minute cores and requested extensions improves packing.
openings.discriminator: Aggregate vacancy proves neither feasibility nor usable capacity; preference information and shorter durations may help only jointly.
openings.fit: Z1 preserves constraints; A1 remains uncertain pending feasible minima and useful durations.
openings.probe: By phone/desk collect needs, windows, equipment and useful durations. Compare inherited, preference-aware 90-minute, flexible-duration inherited-start, and combined schedules for eight weeks. Measure fully met needs, minima, equipment mismatches and preparation time; identify overlapping unmet demand.
openings.uncertainty: Contacts' accuracy, duration/start flexibility and feasible weekly minima are unverified; paper feasibility needs attendance/access confirmation. A minimum slot or undocumented outside rehearsal is not proof of met need.

openings.claim: Test authoritative-ledger read-back against conflicting expectations, then its interaction with preauthorized replacement queues for usable released slots.
openings.discriminator: Ledger consistency addresses stale state; queues identify eligible replacements. Matching confirmations despite conflicts imply other causes.
openings.fit: Preserves constraints; retain phone/desk changes, lock performances/hours, and replace any released weekly minimum before release.
openings.probe: Replay documented changes under queue-only, ledger-only and combined rules; measure placements, conflicting confirmations and handling time. Record accepted changes once, read back room/date/time, timestamp refreshed copies and confirm replacements. Track eight-week conflicts and total administration.
openings.uncertainty: Preauthorization, desk/key access to the ledger and affordable copy/confirmation work remain unverified.

decision: Probe both hypotheses; reject constraint violations. Preserve two rooms, 24 staffed hours, equipment, no new fees and performances. Success requires at least 90% usable needs met, every requested weekly minimum, fewer than two conflicts and average administration at most two hours/week, including elicitation.
